stem: Ammonium iron(II) sulfate, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Fe}(\text{SO}_4)_2$, has a relative formula mass, $M_r$, of 284.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: One of the cations in ammonium iron(II) sulfate is the ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$.
parts.text: One of the cations in ammonium iron(II) sulfate is the ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram of an ammonium ion. Show outer shell electrons only.

Use $\times$ to show electrons from nitrogen.
Use $\bullet$ to show electrons from hydrogen.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the shape of an ammonium ion and predict the bond angle.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: In aqueous solution the ammonium ion acts as a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.
parts.text: In aqueous solution the ammonium ion acts as a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term *weak Brønsted-Lowry acid*.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation to show this behaviour of the ammonium ion in water. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
Mohr's salt, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Fe}(\text{SO}_4)_2\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is the hydrated form of ammonium iron(II) sulfate.

x represents the number of moles of water in 1 mole of the salt.

A student wanted to determine the value of x. $0.784\text{ g}$ of the hydrated salt was dissolved in water and this solution was acidified.

All of the solution was titrated with $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ potassium manganate(VII). $20.0\text{ cm}^3$ of this potassium manganate(VII) solution was required for complete reaction with the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions.
parts.text:
Mohr's salt, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Fe}(\text{SO}_4)_2\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is the hydrated form of ammonium iron(II) sulfate.

x represents the number of moles of water in 1 mole of the salt.

A student wanted to determine the value of x. $0.784\text{ g}$ of the hydrated salt was dissolved in water and this solution was acidified.

All of the solution was titrated with $0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ potassium manganate(VII). $20.0\text{ cm}^3$ of this potassium manganate(VII) solution was required for complete reaction with the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Use changes in oxidation numbers to balance the equation for the reaction taking place.

$\text{MnO}_4^-(\text{aq}) + \text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{H}^+(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
State the role of the $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions in this reaction.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of manganate(VII) ions that reacted.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions in the sample of the salt.

parts.label: (d)(v)
parts.text: Calculate the relative formula mass of $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Fe}(\text{SO}_4)_2\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
